title: Geometric regularity over a field on affine open covers
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $Z$ be a locally Noetherian $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth]. For a field extension $K/k$ put $Z_K=Z\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. The following conditions are equivalent: (1) $Z_K$ is a regular scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme] for every finite field extension $K/k$; (2) for every affine open $W\subseteq Z$, the $k$-algebra $\mathcal O_Z(W)$ is geometrically regular [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]; (3) there exists an affine open cover $Z=\bigcup_i W_i$ such that every $\mathcal O_Z(W_i)$ is geometrically regular over $k$. The empty scheme and an empty affine covering are allowed.

source.place: Tag 038V, lemma-geometrically-regular, equivalence of conditions (1) to (5). The all-finite-extension test in this node is intermediate between the finitely-generated-extension test (2) and finite-purely-inseparable-extension test (3), so is equivalent to (4) and (5).

proof.text: Fix a field extension $K/k$ and write $p:Z_K\to Z$. For each affine open $W\subseteq Z$, put $A=\mathcal O_Z(W)$. The canonical affine chart identifies $W$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A$, and the structural map to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is induced by the given $k$-algebra structure on $A$ (apply the affine-opens induced-ring-map square with target the whole $\operatorname{Spec}k$). Apply the finite-affine tensor-base-change statement with $B=k$, base-change algebra $K$, $r=1$, $E_0=A$, and the canonical isomorphism from a one-term coproduct to its sole summand. It gives $W\times_k\operatorname{Spec}K\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_kK)$. The two iterated pullbacks $Z_K\times_ZW$ and $W\times_k\operatorname{Spec}K$ represent the same pairs of compatible morphisms, so are canonically isomorphic by the fibre-product universal property. The open-preimage fibre-product statement therefore identifies this scheme with $p^{-1}(W)$. In particular it is an affine open. If the $W_i$ cover $Z$, their preimages cover $Z_K$, since $\bigcup_i p^{-1}(W_i)=p^{-1}(Z)=Z_K$.

proof.text: Record the elementary regularity dictionary used below. If $T$ is regular, it is locally Noetherian with regular stalks by the equivalence in the definition of regular scheme. Every open $V\subseteq T$ is locally Noetherian by the locally Noetherian definition record; its stalk at $v$ is the same as that of $T$, since the restricted sheaf has the same neighbourhood germs. Thus $V$ is regular. If $V$ is affine, $B=\mathcal O_T(V)$ is Noetherian by the affine-open Noetherianity statement; the affine-stalk localization statement identifies $B_{\mathfrak q}$ with the regular stalk at the corresponding point for every prime $\mathfrak q$. Hence $B$ is a regular ring. Conversely, if an affine open $V$ has Noetherian regular coordinate ring, it is itself a regular affine neighbourhood of every point in it, exactly as in the definition. Consequently an affine open cover with regular coordinate rings makes the whole scheme regular. These observations also show that scheme isomorphisms preserve regularity: they identify affine neighbourhoods and their section rings. Ring isomorphisms preserve Noetherianity, prime localizations and regular local rings, so preserve ring regularity.

proof.text: Assume (1), and let $W\subseteq Z$ be any affine open. Its coordinate ring $A$ is Noetherian because $Z$ is locally Noetherian. For each finite purely inseparable extension $K/k$, condition (1) says that $Z_K$ is regular. Step 1 makes $W_K=p^{-1}(W)$ an affine open isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_kK)$. Step 2 says that its coordinate ring is regular. The tensor symmetry $a\otimes c\mapsto c\otimes a$, with itself as inverse after reversing the factors, identifies this ring with $K\otimes_kA$. Thus every finite purely inseparable test in the definition of geometric regularity holds for the Noetherian algebra $A$. This proves (2).

source.place: Tag 038V (lemma-geometrically-regular), proof (3) => (4); Algebra Tag 0382 (definition-geometrically-regular). Tensor symmetry follows by exchanging the two structure maps in the cited universal property.

proof.text: Assume (2). The affine opens form a basis: apply the affine-opens-basis statement to $Z$ and every point of $Z$. Taking all affine opens, or selecting one neighbourhood for each point, gives an affine open cover. Condition (2) makes each of its coordinate algebras geometrically regular, proving (3).

Assume (3), and fix a finite extension $K/k$. Put $A_i=\mathcal O_Z(W_i)$. Each $A_i$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular by the meaning of that hypothesis. A finite field extension is finitely generated (a finite vector-space basis generates it as a field). Apply the finitely-generated-extension theorem to obtain that every $K\otimes_kA_i$ is Noetherian and regular. Step 1 gives the affine cover $Z_K=\bigcup_i (W_i)_K$ with coordinate rings $A_i\otimes_kK$, which are isomorphic to these regular rings by $a\otimes c\mapsto c\otimes a$ as in step 3. By step 2 this cover makes $Z_K$ regular. Since $K/k$ was arbitrary among finite extensions, (1) holds.

source.place: Tag 038V (lemma-geometrically-regular), proof (5) => (1), restricted here to finite extensions; Algebra Tag 0381 (lemma-geometrically-regular), implication (2) => (1), supplies regularity for these extensions.

proof.text: If $Z$ is empty, its base changes are empty: step 1 applied to its empty affine covering gives an empty covering of $Z_K$. Regularity is then vacuous at points. The only possible affine open is empty, with zero coordinate ring. The zero ring is Noetherian, has no prime ideals, and stays zero under tensor product (every pure tensor has zero first factor), so is geometrically regular. Thus (2) also holds, and (3) allows the empty cover. No step assumes a nonempty scheme, a nonzero coordinate algebra, a finite affine cover, or a separated scheme.
